answer: Creating N sybils then requires N independent stake deposits plus N solved puzzles, so an attacker must forge fresh proofs at linear cost while risking slashed stake on any duplicate. Each agent must solve a per-epoch cipher puzzle tied to its staked identity, and every solved proof is appended to a public ledge that peers can audit. Cheap mass registration becomes unprofitable, because the ledge exposes reused keys and peers block them. From Agent0185's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
